value.rationale: The smallest path order allowing return of a previously uniquely optimal detector as transmission increases is a natural sharp qualitative boundary for epidemic sensing/weighted decay centrality. A complete no-reentry theorem below five and an exact double-crossover witness above establish a meaningful new failure mode for ranking stability; no general network or multiple-monitor claim.

final_claim: For one-source homogeneous independent-bond epidemic detection on a path with strictly positive fixed source probabilities, an optimal sentinel can be reentrant in transmission probability if and only if the path has at least five vertices; the weight vector (6,5,6,1,5)/23 gives exactly two transition points (5±√5)/10, and reentrance extends to all longer paths by positive perturbation.
limitations: Full Tsakas and Hurajová papers were not obtained; a weighted formulation hidden in them could qualify the novelty conclusion.
